opportunities.title: BTCPay Told You Twice: Patch or Get Drained — Same Flaw, Two News Cycles
opportunities.why_now: BTCPay warned of an actively exploited vulnerability on Aug 7, then had to restrict remote Lightning access by Aug 9 after attackers actually stole funds — a live, unfolding self-custody breach.
opportunities.angle: Timeline breakdown: disclosure → exploitation → emergency mitigation, with a 'why self-hosted Lightning nodes are a soft target' framing and concrete hardening checklist

opportunities.title: Quantum Computers Won't Announce Themselves — Your Wallet Will Just Look Hacked
opportunities.why_now: A Quantus founder is warning that crypto's first real quantum attack will be indistinguishable from ordinary key theft, meaning it may already be happening undetected.
opportunities.angle: Explainer/opinion on how attribution failure is the actual threat model — tie to 'already know how this ends' thesis that legacy ECDSA wallets are sitting ducks

opportunities.title: Kimsuky's AI Upgrade Is the Nation-State Threat Model You Should Be Pricing In
opportunities.why_now: North Korea's Kimsuky group has confirmed it's integrating AI into attacks on crypto and finance targets, escalating an already dominant hacking operation days after the Bybit court ruling on the $1.5B DPRK heist.
opportunities.angle: Threat-actor profile + market angle: what AI-accelerated DPRK tooling means for exchange/custody risk premiums going forward

opportunities.title: Bitcoin's Top Red Teamer Just Switched to Chinese AI — and Called It Gutting
opportunities.why_now: The founder of Bitcoin Red Team publicly admitted turning to Chinese AI tools for vulnerability research, a stark signal about where offensive security capability is actually concentrated.
opportunities.angle: Op-ed on the irony/security implications: US-led open-source Bitcoin security research now dependent on adversarial-nation AI, paired with the parallel story that AI is already surfacing critical exploits across core projects

opportunities.title: Fake CAPTCHAs on BNB Chain: The Oldest Trick Still Draining Wallets in 2026
opportunities.why_now: Hackers are actively using BNB Chain infrastructure to distribute malware disguised as CAPTCHA verification, a low-tech social-engineering vector still succeeding against sophisticated users.
opportunities.angle: Quick-hit security explainer/screenshot breakdown for X thread: how the fake CAPTCHA flow works and the exact clicks that lead to drainer approval
